title: Trigonometry: Problems in Two Dimensions
summary: Solve real-life problems with right-angled triangles, including angles of elevation and depression, and problems that need two triangles.

notes.text: To **solve** a triangle means to find all unknown sides and angles. In a right-angled triangle, use the trigonometric ratios, the theorem of Pythagoras ($c^2 = a^2 + b^2$) and the angle sum ($180^\circ$).

items: Identify the right angle and the angle you are working with.
Label the sides opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse.
Choose the ratio that links the known and unknown values.
Solve, and round only at the end.

notes.text: The angle between the horizontal and the line of sight when you look **up** at an object.
The angle between the horizontal and the line of sight when you look **down** at an object.

notes.caption: The angle of elevation from the observer equals the angle of depression from the top of the tower (alternate angles)

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: The angle of elevation from A to B is equal to the angle of depression from B to A, because they are **alternate angles** between parallel horizontal lines.

notes.title: Worked example 1: elevation
notes.problem: From a point 50 m from the foot of a building, the angle of elevation to the top is $38^\circ$. How tall is the building? (Answer to one decimal place.)
steps: Opposite (height $h$) and adjacent (50 m) are involved, so use tangent.

notes.title: Worked example 2: depression
notes.problem: A lighthouse keeper 60 m above sea level sees a boat at an angle of depression of $14^\circ$. How far is the boat from the foot of the lighthouse?
steps: The angle of elevation from the boat is also $14^\circ$ (alt ∠s).

notes.title: Worked example 3
notes.problem: From point A on level ground the angle of elevation of the top T of a tower is $30^\circ$. From point B, 40 m closer to the tower, the angle of elevation is $50^\circ$. Find the height of the tower.
steps: Let the foot of the tower be F, height $h$ = TF and BF = $x$.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Keep full calculator values in memory between steps; rounding too early can make your final answer wrong.

questions.prompt: The angle of elevation is measured…
The angle of elevation from A to B equals the angle of depression from B to A.
From 20 m away, the angle of elevation to the top of a tree is $42^\circ$. Find the height of the tree, correct to one decimal place.
A ramp is 6 m long and rises 1,2 m. Find the angle the ramp makes with the ground, correct to one decimal place.
From the top of an 80 m cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is $25^\circ$. How far is the boat from the foot of the cliff? Round to the nearest metre.
A rectangular field is 120 m by 50 m. How long is its diagonal?
A kite is flying on a 75 m string at an angle of elevation of $60^\circ$. The string is held 1,5 m above the ground. How high is the kite above the ground?
Two observers are on opposite sides of a 30 m pole, in line with it. Their angles of elevation to the top are $35^\circ$ and $50^\circ$. How far apart are they? Round to one decimal place.
Why should you avoid rounding answers in the middle of a multi-step trigonometry problem?
